n:A&P Investment Fund Management: A&P Investment Fund Management is an asset manager in Macao, meaning a firm that invests money on behalf of clients. Antonio Jose Felix Pontes was Executive Director of the Monetary Authority of Macao, the body that acts as Macao's central bank, and was also Macao Insurance Commissioner and a member of the authority's Advisory Council. He went on to become a board director and Chief Compliance Officer of A&P Investment Fund Management, and a non-executive director of Well Link Bank, Ltd.
n:Alpha Capital Partners: Alpha Capital Partners is an asset manager in Kampala, Uganda, meaning a firm that invests money on behalf of clients. Stephen Mpuuga Kaboyo held senior executive positions at the Bank of Uganda, the country's central bank, and then founded Alpha Capital Partners, where he is Managing Director.
n:Banco Popular de Ahorro: Banco Popular de Ahorro is a bank in Havana, Cuba. Joaquin Alonso Vazquez spent seven years as its vice president, up to 2017, and then served as president of CADECA S.A. From February 2023 he has been Minister President of the Banco Central de Cuba, the island's central bank, which sets Cuba's money policy and issues its currency.
n:Banco Unión S.A. (Bolivia): Banco Union S.A. is a bank in La Paz, Bolivia. Jaime Valencia Valencia worked at the bank, and he has twice been General Manager of the Banco Central de Bolivia, Bolivia's central bank, which issues the country's money: from 1996 to 2006, and again from 16 January 2020.
Banco de Cochabamba S.A. is a bank in the city of Cochabamba, Bolivia. It appears among the financial employers listed on the published career history of Jaime Valencia Valencia, who has been General Manager of the Banco Central de Bolivia, Bolivia's central bank, from 1996 to 2006 and again from 16 January 2020. The 1999 annual report of ASFI, Bolivia's financial regulator, lists Banco de Cochabamba S.A. among entities in liquidation, that is, being wound up.
n:Banque Centrale des Comores strongroom: This is the Banque Centrale des Comores' own strongroom, a secure vault inside the bank, in the capital Moroni. It is where the central bank of the Comoros keeps the gold it owns. The bank's audited accounts for the year ending 31 December 2024 record, in note 5 on gold holdings, eighteen bars held in that strongroom.
n:Belarusbank: Belarusbank is a bank in Minsk, Belarus. Nadezhda Yermakova chaired its board, then chaired the National Bank of Belarus, the country's central bank, from 2011 to 2014. She ran the interim administration of another Minsk bank, Belgazprombank, from 15 June to 11 December 2020, and on 15 January 2021 was appointed head of its board of directors. Belgazprombank's shares are held by Russia's Gazprom PJSC and Gazprombank JSC, 49.66 per cent each, Gazprom Transgaz Belarus with 0.49 per cent and the Belarusian state, through its Ministry of Energy, with 0.097 per cent.
n:Belgazprombank: Belgazprombank is a bank in Minsk, Belarus. Nadezhda Yermakova chaired the National Bank of Belarus, the country's central bank, from 2011 to 2014. On 15 January 2021 she was appointed head of the board of directors of Belgazprombank OJSC.
CADECA S.A. is a company in Havana, Cuba. Joaquin Alonso Vazquez was its president, after seven years as vice president of the bank Banco Popular de Ahorro up to 2017. From February 2023 he has been Minister President of the Banco Central de Cuba, the island's central bank, which issues Cuba's currency and sets its money policy.
n:Caisse Nationale d'Assurance Maladie (: The Caisse Nationale d'Assurance Maladie, or CNAM, is a state agency in Nouakchott that runs health insurance in Mauritania. Abdel Aziz Ould Dahi was its Director General, and in January 2015 he became Governor of the Banque Centrale de Mauritanie, the country's central bank, which issues its money.
n:Central Bank of Iraq vault, Baghdad: This is the Central Bank of Iraq's own vault in Baghdad, where the bank keeps gold it owns. In note 4 of its financial statements for the year ending 31 December 2025, the bank separates its gold into three lines: gold held abroad, gold held in its own vault, and gold coins held in its own vault. The holding kept abroad is much the largest of the three, and is not placed with any named institution.
n:Central Bank of the Russian Federation: These are the Bank of Russia's own vaults, where Russia's central bank keeps the gold it owns. The holding comes to 2,283 tonnes, the sixth largest on this map. The bank's Annual Report 2025 states only that the assets are stored in Russia, without naming where. The bank has itself said, in remarks carried by the news agency Interfax, that it has taken no gold out of the country and that all of it sits in its own storage facilities on Russian territory.
Compania Boliviana de Seguros S.A. is an insurer in La Paz, Bolivia. It appears among the financial employers listed on the published career history of Jaime Valencia Valencia, who has twice been General Manager of the Banco Central de Bolivia, Bolivia's central bank, which issues the country's money: from 1996 to 2006, and again from 16 January 2020.
n:El Nilein Bank: El Nilein Bank is a bank in Khartoum, Sudan. Ibrahim Mohammed Ali Nimir was General Manager of the Central Bank of Sudan, the country's central bank, from 1964 to 1967. He then ran El Nilein Bank as its General Manager from 1970 to 1973, and went back to the central bank as Governor and Chairman of the Board of Directors from 1973 to 1980.
n:Ministry of Trade, Commerce, Industry: This is a government ministry in Port Vila, Vanuatu, covering trade, commerce, industry and tourism. Marakon Alilee was its Director General, and had held senior posts earlier at the Vanuatu Chamber of Commerce, Airports Vanuatu Limited, VANAIR and the Vanuatu National Provident Fund. On 12 September 2014 he was appointed to the board of the Reserve Bank of Vanuatu, the country's central bank.
n:National Bank (Sudan): National Bank is a bank in Khartoum, Sudan. Ibrahim Mohammed Ali Nimir was Governor and Chairman of the Board of Directors of the Central Bank of Sudan, the country's central bank, from 1973 to 1980. He left to become General Manager of National Bank from 1980 to 1982, and later General Manager of Workers National Bank from 1989 to 1992.
n:Seoul Foreign Exchange Brokerage: Seoul Foreign Exchange Brokerage is a brokerage in Seoul, South Korea, meaning a firm that arranges currency trades between other institutions. Jeong Gyu-il joined the Bank of Korea, the country's central bank, in 1987 and rose to Deputy Governor. His appointment as chief executive and president of Seoul Foreign Exchange Brokerage was announced on 2 July 2021.
n:Well Link Bank: Well Link Bank is a bank in Macao. Antonio Jose Felix Pontes was Executive Director of the Monetary Authority of Macao, the body that acts as Macao's central bank, and was also Macao Insurance Commissioner and a member of the authority's Advisory Council. He went on to become a Non-Executive Director of Well Link Bank, Ltd., and a board director and Chief Compliance Officer of the asset manager A&P Investment Fund Management.
n:Workers National Bank (Sudan): Workers National Bank is a bank in Khartoum, Sudan. Ibrahim Mohammed Ali Nimir was Governor and Chairman of the Board of Directors of the Central Bank of Sudan, the country's central bank, from 1973 to 1980. He then served as General Manager of National Bank from 1980 to 1982, and as General Manager of Workers National Bank from 1989 to 1992.
